children: said Tuesday it signed an agreement to supply 280 megawatts of electrolyzers for Arcadia eFuels’ planned sustainable aviation fuel project in Denmark, while also becoming the preferred supplier for a pipeline of additional projects totaling more than 1 gigawatt.

The initial agreement covers Arcadia’s Project ENDOR at the Port of Vordingborg. The facility would use renewable electricity to power Plug’s GenEco electrolyzers, producing about 110 tons of hydrogen a day. Arcadia plans to combine the hydrogen with captured carbon dioxide to produce synthetic aviation fuel, or e-SAF, that can be used in conventional aircraft.
For investors, the agreement gives Plug

a potentially significant source of future electrolyzer demand, but much of that opportunity remains conditional. Deliveries for the 280 MW ENDOR project will not begin until a notice to proceed is issued, and the project has not yet reached a final investment decision. The additional 1 GW-plus pipeline represents potential business rather than firm orders, making project financing and construction decisions important milestones to watch.
Under a separate cooperation agreement, Plug

will be the preferred electrolyzer supplier for four additional Arcadia projects planned in Europe and the Americas. Arcadia will also receive priority access to Plug’s manufacturing capacity as those developments progress.

Project ENDOR is advancing toward a final investment decision after about three years of engineering work between the companies. Plug said the supply agreement represents one of the project documents completed as Arcadia works toward that decision.

The project is aimed partly at demand created by European aviation regulations. The EU’s ReFuelEU Aviation rules require sustainable aviation fuels to account for an increasing portion of fuel supplied at European airports, with separate requirements for synthetic aviation fuels beginning in 2030.

is already working on electrolyzer projects in several European markets, including a 100 MW installation at Galp’s Sines refinery in Portugal. The Arcadia agreements would expand its exposure to the emerging market for hydrogen-derived aviation fuels if the planned projects secure financing and proceed to construction.
